about: The shape of every REST answer the Twins page reads (all routes under /api/plugins/grok-bot-twin).
Checked three ways: the built-in sample, a real twin through the botport helper (tests/test_api_contract.py)
and the mock answers of the page's own assertion suite (tests/desktop/contract.mjs).
Types: str, int, number, bool, null, dict, list, any; a shape name; list[TYPE]; a union A|B.
required: the key must be there and fit. optional: the key may be missing, but must fit when it is there.
backend: keys every backend answer also carries (required there); the page's test mock may leave them out.
Backend answers may carry other keys unless a shape says closed: true. The page's test mock may never carry
a key that is not listed here: a mock must not invent what the backend does not send.
Words and wording are not checked here.
Source: what the Twins page needs, and what dashboard/plugin_api.py + twin/service.py really return.

ErrorEnvelope.route: any route, HTTP 200, when the service reports a problem (bad input and unknown twin included)

ErrorBody.note: lines: only on a refused paste of instructions (code looks_like_secret): the 1-based line numbers, never the text

FastCheck.note: on: a changed name or description in Grok is picked up right away in this Hermes process (else it waits for the timed check, interval_s). mode: events (the system wakes the plugin), poll (file dates every 2 s) or off

Engine.note: the last four are there only while a helper file is found

SetupBrief.note: ready: botport usable AND the Grok desktop app found. cause: grok_app | botport_missing | botport_unverified | no_build | null (the machine-readable twin of problem)

Pair.route: GET /status pairs[i]; also POST /twins/create pairs[i] and POST /demo pairs[i]
Pair.note: setup_left: what is left before the twin is finished, a subset of [instructions, model] in that order. model_hint: only while model is left

PairHermes.note: model_from: default (copied when the twin was made and not changed since) | own | null (no model)

SetupCheck.note: method: pinned (the plugin's own table) | gh (GitHub's build record) | local (accepted in the terminal without a check) | null

Parity.note: passed/total are null only when the helper is too old to compare (then `note` says so)

ParityCheck.note: why: one plain sentence for the list (22 words at most, no brackets, no command); detail is botport's own text and belongs under Technical details

RestorePoint.note: text: that version (password-like lines hidden, 20 kB at most), null when the plugin cannot show it. replaced_by: paste | grok | choice | put_back | send | import | null

SkillSyncSetup.route: POST /pairs/{id}/skill-sync (a shared folder; nothing for the remembered one; remake for the set-up folder again)
SkillSyncSetup.note: via: kit (the sync bot is set up by chat, with the set-up folder) | inbox (a later twin: through the shared folder, nothing to do in Grok)

SkillSyncKit.note: folder: null for the sample. missing: release files the owner still has to download (the plugin downloads nothing)

SkillSyncStatus.note: heartbeat: a ready sentence (Skill sync last ran 12 min ago). Read from one small file the sync bot's script writes into the shared folder

SkillSyncBox.note: the botport the sync bot runs in its box, against the release this computer runs

Event.note: payload depends on the event type

SetupDownload.note: the direct release file for this computer; found: the download seen in the Downloads folder (by exact name), dir: that folder (for the file picker only)

SkillText.note: item=description: the twin's description as it is in Hermes (name is then "description"; item comes back as the twin's own id for it)

FleetBrief.note: role: none | source | follower. machines: how many OTHER machines. source: on a follower only

PairFleet.route: GET /status pairs[i].fleet, on a machine that shares

Fleet.route: GET /fleet; also the answer of POST /fleet/share, /fleet/link, /fleet/name, /fleet/sync, /fleet/removed/{rid}/restore

Machine.note: id: m- and 12 hex. platform: macos | linux | windows | other

Share.note: state: off | on | starting | error. network: tailscale | lan | loopback

Source.note: state: syncing | in_sync | offline | sharing_off | error

FleetMachine.note: state: in_sync | behind | offline | never_synced | unknown

FleetTwin.note: state: in_sync | error | not_listed. changed_at, changed (on a linked computer only): when this twin's first copy, or a new name or description of it, last arrived on this computer, and which: new | name | description (description when both changed)

FleetTwinMachine.note: state: in_sync | behind | offline | pending | unknown. pending: only on the sharing machine, for a linked machine that has never reported holding this twin (made while it was off or while sharing was off): the twin is on its way there, not there. error: only on the sharing machine, for a machine that reported it could not make this twin

Leaving.route: POST /fleet/unlink and POST /fleet/machines/{id}/remove (dry run and for real)

SetupExportInfo.note: request: the text the owner pastes into the bot's own Grok chat to ask for its setup export. privacy: the one sentence about memories and facts. last: the last import into this twin (when, and the connector names it listed to set up on this computer), null before the first

SetupExport.note: apply false: what an import of this file would do (nothing is changed or kept). apply true: what it did. added: routines added by this call (0 on a preview). The file's text is never stored; memories and facts about the owner are left out and only counted

SetupExportBot.note: matches: the export's bot has this twin's Grok name

SetupExportInstructions.note: state: new | same | none | held. left_out: 1-based numbers of the lines left out because they look like a password or key (never the text). text: the instructions as they would be saved, made safe to show. why: "" unless state is held and the backend has its own sentence

SetupExportRoutine.note: state on a preview: new | exists | held | manual; after an import: added | failed | exists | held | manual. why: the plain reason for manual and failed (the page has its own words for the other states)

SetupExportConnector.note: a name to set up on this computer; never an address or a login

SetupExportLeftOut.note: counts only. routines: those beyond the first 50 in the file, which were not read

BatchInfo.note: the sheet for several new twins. request/privacy: as SetupExportInfo. default_model: the default Hermes profile's model id ("" when none). models: distinct model ids in use on this Hermes, default first, at most 20. twins: every twin, or the ones named. downloads.label is a word, never the folder's path

BatchTwin.note: name: the Grok bot's name. left: what the twin still needs, of instructions | model. model: its model id ("" when none)

BatchPickup.note: where answer files are watched for. via: mirror (skill sync is set up: the shared folder's exports/ and Downloads; request asks each bot to save its file in the box too) | downloads. label is words, never a path

BatchEndpoint.note: a model server already set up in the default Hermes profile's config.yaml, at most 6; GET <base_url>/models answered (reachable) or not, 2 s, no key sent. base_url_label is host:port only. models: at most 20 ids

BatchSkillSync.note: set_up: the guided skill sync has its shared folder; pair_ids: the twins it carries

ComputerUse.note: can Hermes do the Grok part itself (twin/grok_part.py). enable: sentences saying exactly what to enable. why: "" or why not

GrokPart.note: ok: the flow is on and message is the chat text for Hermes; else status says what to enable

SetModel.note: state: set | same | sample (the sample twin is never written)

BatchModelResult.note: state: set | same | sample | failed; why: the reason when failed, else ""

BatchMatch.note: one match per bot in a file that has a ticked twin, else one row for the file. The file's text is never stored or echoed

BatchMatchRow.note: state: matched | no_twin | not_export | ambiguous. name: the twin's bot name ("" without a twin). bot: the bot's name in the file

BatchImportRow.note: one per ticked twin. state: done | failed | no_file | sample (and ready: a Downloads look with apply false). routines: added switched off. lines_left_out: lines of the instructions left out because they look like a password or key

BatchDownloads.note: files: setup exports in Downloads since then. results: imports done by this call. waiting: ticked twins no file is for yet
